questions.explanation: A shared, standards-based tool endpoint lets many agents reuse one integration while a central layer enforces who may call what. Copies, open access or scraping multiply maintenance and risk.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: A vector search applies a very selective metadata filter (one tenant among thousands) after retrieving the top 10 nearest neighbors, and often returns zero results. What is the fix?

options.A: Remove the metadata filter and let the model discard other tenants' passages while it writes the final answer
options.B: Lower the embedding dimension, since fewer dimensions make more vectors fall inside the filtered subset
options.C: Apply the filter during the nearest-neighbor search, using the engine's filtered or pre-filtered search, so the top-k is drawn from matching vectors only
options.D: Keep post-filtering but raise k to 10,000 permanently, which guarantees that matching vectors always appear in the candidate set

questions.explanation: Post-filtering discards most candidates when the filter is selective. Filtering inside the search finds the nearest vectors among only the allowed ones, and leaving isolation to the model would expose other tenants' data.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: Web pages crawled for a knowledge base contain navigation menus, footers and cookie banners, and these repeated fragments dominate retrieval results. What should be done?

options.A: Increase chunk size so the boilerplate is a smaller fraction of every chunk, and leave it in the index otherwise
options.B: Lower the number of retrieved results to one, so that boilerplate can appear at most a single time in the results
options.C: Embed the boilerplate more times so it becomes an accepted part of what the vector space considers normal
options.D: Extract the main content and strip boilerplate before chunking, so that the index contains only meaningful text from each page

questions.explanation: Repeated boilerplate creates near-duplicate chunks that match many queries. Removing it during preprocessing keeps the index focused, while tweaking size or counts hides but does not remove the noise.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: A team stores unit-normalized embeddings but configures the index with L2 distance, while a tutorial suggested cosine. What is true about this situation?

options.A: Normalization removes the need for a distance metric altogether, so the index is able to return results without any configured measure at all
options.B: L2 distance and cosine similarity always disagree with each other, so the results returned from the index will be wrong for any kind of embedding
options.C: L2 distance can be applied only to images, so text embeddings cannot be searched with it under any circumstance, whether normalized or not
options.D: For unit-normalized vectors, cosine, inner product and L2 give the same ranking, but using L2 on unnormalized vectors could change the order

questions.explanation: On unit vectors these metrics are monotonic transformations of each other, so rankings agree. Without normalization, magnitude affects L2 and inner product differently from cosine.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: Product data lives in a relational database and changes constantly, and the RAG index must reflect updates and deletions within minutes. Which pipeline is most appropriate?

options.A: Embed new rows only, and never delete the vectors for removed rows, since stale vectors have no effect on the quality of the answers users receive
options.B: Capture changes with a stream or CDC, embed changed records, upsert the vectors, and remove vectors for deleted records with explicit delete events
options.C: Ask users to report wrong answers, then manually edit the vector index by hand for each of the individual cases that are reported to the team
options.D: Rebuild the whole vector index from scratch every night and accept that answers shown to users may be up to a full day out of date

questions.explanation: Change streams keep the index synchronized within minutes, and handling deletes prevents stale content from being served. Nightly rebuilds, ignoring deletes and manual fixes fail the freshness requirement.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: A large archive of rarely queried embeddings is inflating the cost of a high-performance vector store, while recent data is queried constantly. Which strategy cuts cost with little impact on users?

options.A: Delete the oldest vectors regardless of how often they are queried, since old content is never valuable to any of the users of the system
options.B: Duplicate the whole archive into a second high-performance store so that queries are split evenly between the two copies to share the load
options.C: Tier the data: keep hot vectors in the low-latency store and move cold vectors to lower-cost vector storage such as S3 Vectors, querying it as needed
options.D: Move all of the vectors to the cheapest store, including the constantly queried ones, and simply accept the slower responses that will result

questions.explanation: Access patterns differ by age, so placing data on storage that matches its query frequency lowers cost while keeping the hot path fast. Deleting or duplicating data hurts coverage or raises cost.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: An e-commerce site wants shoppers to search product photos using text queries such as "red leather handbag". Which architecture is most direct?

options.A: Embed the images with an audio embedding model, then compare them with text queries using keyword matching
options.B: Embed product images and text queries with a multimodal embedding model into one vector space, then run similarity search
options.C: Use a text-only embedding model on the image file names, and ignore the image content completely
options.D: Store the raw image bytes as text in the vector index and let the query match the bytes directly

questions.explanation: A multimodal embedding model places images and text in a shared space, enabling text-to-image similarity. Audio models, raw bytes or file names do not capture visual content.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: An organization must ingest PDFs, images, audio and video into a RAG pipeline and wants consistent structured output without building a separate extraction stack for each type. Which service targets this?

options.A: Amazon CloudFront, which extracts fields from documents while caching them at edge locations
options.B: Amazon Route 53, which converts media files into text records by resolving their names
options.C: Amazon Bedrock Data Automation, which extracts insights from documents, images, audio and video into structured output
options.D: AWS Direct Connect, which parses the contents of media files as they travel over the dedicated link

questions.explanation: Bedrock Data Automation is built to turn multimodal content into structured results that downstream pipelines can use. The other services handle DNS, networking or content delivery.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: Users cannot verify RAG citations, and engineers struggle to debug bad retrievals, because chunks lack provenance. Which indexing practice fixes this?

options.A: Remove all identifiers from chunks so the model cannot be biased by the origin of the text it reads
options.B: Store metadata such as source URI, page number and section with each chunk, and return it alongside the retrieved text
options.C: Store only the embedding vectors and discard the original text, since the model can reconstruct the source on demand
options.D: Put every document into one file so that the source of any chunk is always the same single file

questions.explanation: Provenance metadata makes citations checkable and retrieval problems traceable. Discarding text or identifiers removes the information needed to show or verify sources.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Before launching a public assistant, the security team wants a repeatable way to test resistance to jailbreaks, prompt injection and PII extraction. Which approach is best?

options.A: Ask a colleague to try to break the assistant informally, and record only the attacks that succeeded on the first attempt
options.B: Test manually once with a few obvious attack phrases the night before launch, and assume the results will hold from then on
options.C: Rely on the foundation model provider's safety training alone, and skip application-level adversarial testing entirely
options.D: Maintain an adversarial test suite of attack prompts, run it automatically in CI and after changes, and track the attack success rate over time

questions.explanation: Attack surfaces change with prompts, tools and data, so red-team tests must be systematic and repeatable. One-off or informal testing and reliance on provider training leave gaps.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: A company fine-tunes a model on customer support transcripts that contain names, emails and account numbers. Which precaution is most important?

options.A: Publish the training data in a public bucket so that the customization job can read it without running into any permission issues at all
options.B: Rely on an output guardrail as the only control, and leave the training data itself completely unchanged in storage for later jobs to use
options.C: Remove or mask PII from the training data first, since models can memorize and reproduce training content, and run the job with encryption and network controls
options.D: Train on the raw transcripts as they are, because fine-tuned models never reproduce any of the examples they were trained on in later responses

questions.explanation: Fine-tuned models can regurgitate training data, so personal information should be removed before training. Encryption and network isolation protect the job, but do not undo memorization.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: A public chat API is called by anonymous scripts that send extremely long prompts in loops, and the bill spikes. Which combination of controls best mitigates this denial-of-wallet risk?

options.A: Allow anonymous access but raise the account quota, so that all of the abusive requests can be served without throttling
options.B: Require authentication, enforce per-user rate limits and input length caps, add WAF rules, and alert on spend with budgets
options.C: Disable CloudWatch metrics, which removes the visibility that attackers rely on to tune their prompts
options.D: Increase maxTokens for all users so that responses to abusive prompts finish faster and cost less per request

questions.explanation: Abuse controls sit in front of the model: identify callers, cap request size and rate, filter traffic and alert on cost. Raising quotas or output limits increases exposure.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: A model's answer is inserted directly into a SQL string and into an HTML page by the application. What secure-design principle is violated, and what is the fix?

options.A: Model output is untrusted input, so use parameterized queries and output encoding or sanitization instead of concatenating it directly
options.B: Nothing is violated, because model output is generated by AWS and is therefore safe to insert into any interpreter
options.C: The fix is to ask the model to promise that its output contains no code, and to trust the promise for all requests
options.D: The only fix is to lower the temperature to zero, which prevents the model from ever producing special characters

questions.explanation: Attackers can steer model output, so it must be handled like any user input. Parameterization and encoding stop injection, whereas trust or promises do not.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: A regulated workload must keep all inference within a single AWS Region for residency reasons. Which combination supports this requirement?

options.A: Invoke models in that Region directly, avoid cross-Region inference profiles for this workload, and use service control policies to deny Bedrock use in other Regions
options.B: Use a cross-Region inference profile that may route requests to any Region, because the routing is transparent to the application and does not matter for residency
options.C: Rely on the application code to add a comment stating that the data must not leave the Region, and trust the platform to comply with it
options.D: Store the prompts in the required Region, and allow model invocation in whichever other Region happens to have free capacity at that moment

questions.explanation: Residency requires that inference itself stays in-Region. Direct regional invocation, avoiding cross-Region routing and organization-level guardrails on Region use enforce that, unlike comments or capacity-based routing.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: A private subnet workload must call Bedrock only for the company's own approved models and only by approved roles, even if credentials are stolen and used from inside the VPC. Which control adds this perimeter?

options.A: A VPC endpoint policy that restricts which principals and actions may use the endpoint, combined with IAM policies
options.B: A CloudWatch dashboard that displays approved models, since visibility prevents unapproved calls from succeeding
options.C: A public S3 bucket policy that lists the approved model names, which Bedrock reads before every invocation
options.D: An internet gateway route with a security group that allows all outbound traffic on port 443 for every instance

questions.explanation: Endpoint policies apply an additional resource-side check on traffic that passes through the endpoint, creating a data perimeter. Open routes, unrelated bucket policies and dashboards do not restrict calls.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Production prompts are stored in Prompt Management, and an engineer's quick edit to a live prompt caused an incident. Which governance approach is best?

options.A: Grant everyone administrator access to prompts so that incidents can be fixed immediately by whichever person happens to notice them first
options.B: Treat prompts as code: restrict edit permissions with IAM, require review for new versions, and let production reference only approved immutable versions
options.C: Allow every developer to edit the production prompt directly, because speed of change matters far more than change control in a fast-moving team
options.D: Keep the prompts in an unversioned text file on a shared drive so that no one is able to accidentally change the version that is deployed

questions.explanation: Prompts change model behavior, so they need the same controls as code: least-privilege permissions, review and immutable versions in production. Open editing or unversioned files remove traceability.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Users upload photos to a multimodal assistant. The existing guardrail evaluates only text, and an audit finds violent imagery passing through. What should be added?

options.A: Increase the text word filter list, because filtering more words also filters the pixels of an uploaded photo
options.B: Lower the image resolution before upload, since low-resolution images are never able to contain harmful content
options.C: Enable content filters that support image inputs in the guardrail, so uploaded images are evaluated as well as text
options.D: Ask the model in the system prompt not to look at violent photos, and consider the risk fully eliminated

questions.explanation: A text-only policy cannot inspect image content. Guardrail content filters that support images screen the visual input, unlike word lists, instructions or downscaling.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: A pipeline sends every step, including trivial classification, to the largest model, and costs are high. Some steps need deep reasoning and most do not. Which pattern reduces cost while preserving quality?

options.A: Use a model cascade: handle routine steps with a smaller, cheaper model and escalate to the larger one only when confidence is low or the task is complex
options.B: Alternate between the small and the large models at random for each request so that cost and quality average out reasonably over time
options.C: Use the largest model for every step, and reduce the cost by shortening all of the outputs to a single word regardless of the task
options.D: Use the smallest model for every step, including the reasoning-heavy ones, and simply accept whatever quality results from that single choice

questions.explanation: Cascading applies the cheapest capable model to each step and reserves expensive capacity for hard cases. Uniform choices either waste money or hurt quality, and random alternation does neither reliably.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: A request needs a user profile lookup, a retrieval query and an input guardrail check, which run one after another and add up to 1.8 seconds before generation. What is the best optimization?

options.A: Run the independent steps concurrently, since none depends on another's output, and start generation once the results are ready
options.B: Remove the input guardrail check for all users, because skipping safety controls is always the fastest optimization
options.C: Increase the temperature so that generation begins earlier and the earlier steps become unnecessary
options.D: Merge the three steps into one bigger sequential step, so that the total time is spent in a single place

questions.explanation: Independent calls can overlap, so latency becomes roughly the slowest step instead of the sum. Removing safety checks or changing sampling does not address sequential waiting.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: Answer quality drops after a release, but engineers cannot tell whether the prompt, model, retrieval settings or index changed. What logging practice makes such regressions diagnosable?

options.A: Record identifiers such as prompt version, model ID, retrieval settings, index version and token usage with each request, so behavior can be compared before and after
options.B: Log only the final answer text and discard everything else, because reproducing a failure requires nothing beyond the output that the user saw
options.C: Log only the temperature setting, since sampling is the only factor that can ever change the quality of an answer that is returned
options.D: Log nothing in production, and reproduce any problems later by simply asking the same question again in the console when someone reports it

questions.explanation: Tagging each request with the configuration that produced it lets you correlate quality changes with specific releases. Output-only logs or no logs leave the cause unknowable.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: A nightly job of 2 million non-urgent summarization requests keeps exhausting on-demand quotas, delaying interactive users. Which change protects the interactive traffic?

options.A: Give the nightly job a higher temperature so that its requests use fewer tokens and therefore stay comfortably below the quota limits
options.B: Disable retries in the nightly job, which lets it consume the whole quota quickly without any of the delays that come with backoff
options.C: Run the nightly job in the middle of the day so that it overlaps with peak interactive usage and therefore finishes sooner than at night
options.D: Move the nightly job to batch inference, which does not compete with interactive on-demand capacity, and process results asynchronously from S3

questions.explanation: Batch inference is designed for large asynchronous workloads and separates them from real-time traffic, while shifting work to peak hours or removing backoff makes contention worse.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: Invocation logging sends full prompts, which include large retrieved contexts and images, to CloudWatch Logs, and the logging bill exceeds the inference bill. Which adjustment is most appropriate?

options.A: Log each prompt ten times to different destinations so that at least one of the copies is cheap to store
options.B: Deliver large payloads to S3 instead, sample or limit what is logged, and set retention so storage does not grow indefinitely
options.C: Keep logging everything to CloudWatch Logs forever, since log volume never has a meaningful effect on total spending
options.D: Disable all monitoring for the application, including the metrics and alarms that do not depend on the logged prompts

questions.explanation: Log volume and retention drive cost. Routing large payloads to inexpensive storage, sampling and lifecycle rules control it while keeping useful observability. Disabling monitoring or duplicating logs does not.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: A serverless chat backend waits for the complete model response before returning it, so users stare at a blank screen for several seconds. Which change improves perceived latency the most?

options.A: Increase the Lambda memory so the function generates tokens more quickly than the model itself is able to produce them
options.B: Lower maxTokens to one so that the response always returns immediately, whatever the question asks
options.C: Add a second model call that repeats the answer so that the first call appears to finish sooner
options.D: Use the streaming API and stream tokens to the client as they arrive, for example with Lambda response streaming or a WebSocket connection

questions.explanation: Streaming lets users start reading while generation continues, cutting time to first visible output. More memory does not speed up the model, and truncating or duplicating calls harms the answer.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: Some responses end mid-sentence in production, even though the calls succeed with HTTP 200. What should the application check and do?

options.A: Inspect the stop reason in the response; a max_tokens stop indicates truncation, so raise the limit or handle continuation instead of returning the partial text
options.B: Retry the same request indefinitely until a response happens to be complete, without changing any of the request parameters between attempts
options.C: Lower the temperature to zero, which always forces the model to finish its final sentence before it decides to stop generating output
options.D: Ignore the stop reason entirely, since an HTTP 200 status code guarantees that the model has produced a complete answer to the request

questions.explanation: A successful call can still be cut off by the output limit. The stop reason reveals this, allowing the application to adjust or continue. Sampling and blind retries do not fix a length cap.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: A multi-turn assistant sends the entire conversation history with every request, and after 40 turns the cost and latency of each call have grown sharply. Which strategy is best?

options.A: Keep a sliding window of recent turns plus a running summary of older ones, and cache the stable prefix such as system instructions
options.B: Ask the user to restart the chat every three messages, and do not preserve any information between restarts
options.C: Keep sending the entire history forever, because the context window makes long conversations free of any cost
options.D: Delete the conversation after every single turn, so that the assistant never remembers anything the user said before

questions.explanation: Trimming with summarization bounds input size while preserving key context, and caching the stable prefix cuts repeated processing. Full history is billed every turn, and forgetting everything breaks the experience.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: Users notice subtle quality shifts although the team changed nothing. The application calls a model alias that resolves to whatever the provider considers the latest version. What is the best practice?

options.A: Pin to a specific model version identifier, and test and promote new versions deliberately using your evaluation suite
options.B: Disable evaluations, since unchanged application code proves that the output quality cannot have changed
options.C: Switch models every week at random, so that no single version's quirks are seen by users for long
options.D: Keep using the floating alias, because providers guarantee that every update is fully backward compatible for all prompts

questions.explanation: Floating references can change behavior without any code change. Pinning versions and promoting after testing makes upgrades intentional and reversible.
